meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who gave my son a zero before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on, Hale.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend, and pasting a finished draft into a new file proves nothing. Show me the history itself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record, and it stays out of his classroom.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember quotations all the time, Hale. A bad citation is a careless mistake, not proof of anything.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's what an outline is for. Put both on the desk. And you still haven't answered me on the quotation.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
A nervous kid cornered by his teacher, a day before a zero, couldn't recite his own phrasing on the spot. Show me the note. Then tell me what you're actually proposing.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against a weekend at home, of course they read differently. I asked what you're proposing.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then it has no business being said in this room. Put your offer on the table, or I'm walking down the hall to the principal.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, supervised, nowhere near his classmates, and marked in time for his December 1 applications. I want the promise that nothing goes on his file in an email from you before I'm out of the parking lot.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. Provided it's marked before December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. Put the day, the room and who's supervising in that email. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes, and Thursday, marked well before December 1. I'll be reading that email tonight.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Who else has seen that checker report?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 after school, that its mark will replace the zero and be in before December 1, and that nothing will go on his record. I still expect that promise in writing, along with the room, the supervisor, and an answer on who else has seen the checker report. I expect your email tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing tonight plus an answer on who else saw the checker report; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her call cut the meeting short.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times on the night of October 28 moved her first, because it was dated, specific, tied to Owen's own file and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Bringing up the checker score after your case was already strong gained you nothing and gave her an opening to threaten the principal, because to her a detector number is a machine's guess.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placing the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due landed very close to that memory, which proves nothing about the essay but is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she called the invented Hamlet line a careless student mistake, answer that point directly before moving on to the outline, so no defence of hers is left standing.
